B.explanation: Uses the full $60.0^{\circ}$ as $\theta$ and $n=2$, giving $\lambda = d\sin60.0^{\circ}/2 \approx 498 \text{ nm}$, which misreads both angle and order.

Recall the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ where $\theta$ is measured from the central maximum to the $n$th order maximum.
Halve $60.0^{\circ}$ to get $\theta$ for $n=1$, then calculate $\lambda = (1.15 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m})\sin\theta$ and convert to $\text{nm}$.
walkthrough: The slit spacing is $d = 1.15 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and the order is $n = 1$ because first-order maxima are observed.
The diagram shows $60.0^{\circ}$ from the upper first-order beam to the lower first-order beam, symmetric about the incident light direction.
So the diffraction angle for one first-order maximum is half of this: $\theta = 60.0^{\circ}/2 = 30.0^{\circ}$.
Use the diffraction grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $n=1$: $\lambda = d\sin30.0^{\circ}$.
Convert to nanometres: $5.75 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 575 \text{ nm}$. This is option C.
